project_type: Expo SDK 54 custom-dev-build React Native + TypeScript app (iOS-focused). Phase 1 shipped a content/domain/ui split, a compile-only Swift focus native module, a pure loadCatalog parser, and four typed domain placeholders throwing NotImplementedError. Phase 2 turns the placeholders into real tested logic, enriches the content, adds local persistence, and replaces the single placeholder Home screen with a full learning-journey navigation graph. Native code does NOT change this phase.
language: TypeScript 5.9.3 (strict). React 19.1.0 / React Native 0.81.5 (SDK 54 matrix). Domain layer is PURE TS (no react/react-native/AsyncStorage/Node-IO imports).
build_system: npm on Node v20.19.4, lockfile package-lock.json. Quirk: expo/tsconfig.base already sets resolveJsonModule:true so content/tracks.json imports typecheck without config changes. The only new runtime dependency allowed this phase is @react-native-async-storage/async-storage pinned EXACTLY to 2.2.0 (verified in node_modules/expo/bundledNativeModules.json). Add it with NO caret.
test_framework: jest via jest-expo@54.0.18 preset (jest.config.js preset 'jest-expo' with a transformIgnorePatterns allowlist for RN/Expo/react-navigation). Tests live in __tests__/. react-test-renderer@19.1.0 is ALREADY installed (use it for screen render smoke tests). @testing-library/react-native is NOT installed and must NOT be added (outside the pinned matrix). jest-expo does not auto-mock AsyncStorage: in persistence/screen tests register jest.mock('@react-native-async-storage/async-storage', () => require('@react-native-async-storage/async-storage/jest/async-storage-mock')). Pure domain tests need ZERO mocks.

environment_constraints: macOS, Node v20.19.4. Git: branch main, local-only, NO remote, NO worktree in use here (work on main); commit locally only when the FEAT's verification is green; NEVER push; never --amend/force. Keep .kiro and the ios/ prebuild artifact untouched. HARD product constraints from the design: honest state everywhere (no fabricated percentages/badges); focus protection reuses the Phase 1 availability truth and is UNAVAILABLE in this environment (never fake a blocked/active state or simulate blocking with a JS timer); certificates are a labeled PREVIEW only (PDF is Phase 6); finance content is educational-only with a required disclaimer; XP/streak stays Phase 4 (Phase 2 emits only idempotent completion events, no XP accrual); corrupt local store fails safe to defaults; deletion wipes the single goalie.v1 key completely.
key_patterns: content/domain/ui separation: src/domain/ is PURE TS. loadCatalog(raw: unknown): Catalog re-validates fail-fast and never returns partials; its invariants MIRROR scripts/validate-catalog.mjs (keep the two in sync). Content collections are uniformly readonly arrays. Progression is a pure reducer over plain-JSON state keyed `${trackId}/${levelId}`; the monotonic non-regression invariant (completeLesson only adds; recordMasteryResult OR's masteryPassed and max's bestCorrectCount; no clear API) lives in the domain layer and is unit-tested without mocks. Derived reads (isLevelComplete/viewLevelProgress) take a Level and compute `${trackId}/${level.id}` — the SAME key the writers used. Assessment grading is deterministic: correct iff answers[i]===questions[i].correctIndex; passed iff correctCount>=MASTERY_PASS_THRESHOLD(4); length mismatch throws AssessmentError; out-of-range selectedIndex grades as incorrect (not an error). Error classes are named like Phase 1's CatalogError (AssessmentError, ProgressionError). Focus availability: async with sync guards first; REASON_TEXT reason->copy map is currently PRIVATE inside src/ui/screens/HomeScreen.tsx and must be extracted to a shared src/ui/focus/reasonText.ts. Persistence is the ONLY AsyncStorage importer; all logic it wraps is in the pure domain layer. App.tsx is the single composition root above RootNavigator; index.ts only registerRootComponent(App) and stays unchanged. RootNavigator owns RootStackParamList + NavigationContainer and accepts a computed initialRouteName prop.
